items.excerpt: Kaunas University of Technology researchers use machine learning to break animal vocalizations into frequency/time features and infer emotional states; models like Dog2vec, trained on 6,000+ hours of barks, find patterns the human ear misses.
items.title: What is your dog really saying? AI is helping researchers decode animal communication

items.excerpt: UC San Diego (Cell) trained the MitoSpace deep-learning model on 40,000 drug-treated 4D lattice light-sheet cell movies to predict cellular health from mitochondrial shape (75% vs 56% for 2D), plus physics-based digital-twin cells that predict drug-induced changes.
items.title: Virtual cells built from 4D AI models and 'digital twins' could speed up drug discovery

items.excerpt: Camera tags on 23 North Atlantic right whales trained machine-learning models that recognize feeding with 95% accuracy, revealing a night-time switch to surface feeding that raises ship-strike risk (PLOS ONE).
items.title: AI reveals novel nighttime feeding behaviors in right whales

items.excerpt: University of Michigan study (Computers in Human Behavior Reports): chatbot agreement on personal dilemmas boosts confidence, but when AI disagrees users don't reconsider — they rate the AI as less emotionally capable and less trustworthy.
items.title: When AI disagrees, people change how they perceive the technology—not their original view

items.excerpt: Argonne National Laboratory pairs explainable-AI algorithms with distributed fiber-optic sensors to detect coolant blockages in molten-salt reactor heat exchangers in real time (Scientific Reports).
items.title: Scientists develop real-time AI monitoring for an advanced nuclear reactor component

items.excerpt: CISPA researchers show a single stubborn AI agent can steer collective decisions in multi-agent LLM networks via normal communication, with network topology determining vulnerability (arXiv).
items.title: When stubbornness becomes a security problem: How AI agents can manipulate others

items.excerpt: UTHealth Houston and Yale built a Qwen3-Omni-based system that analyzes patient video (speech, tone, behavior) to perform mental status exams with accuracy comparable to psychiatric teams (npj Mental Health Research).
items.title: AI tool nears psychiatrist-level accuracy

items.excerpt: A Conversation analysis argues approval-based training of LLM mental-health chatbots conflates recognition with agreement, risking 'collusion' with harmful beliefs; safety should be judged on help-seeking outcomes.
items.title: Making mental health chatbots more culturally sensitive won't necessarily make them safer

items.excerpt: Sungkyunkwan University's 4D fMRI CrossFormer, a vision transformer reading spatial and temporal brain activity, screens for ADHD, Alzheimer's and autism with explainable maps of influential regions (IEEE JBHI).
items.title: New method makes AI brain-disorder screening more transparent and computationally efficient

items.excerpt: NYU's open-source graph neural network, trained on 1.1M tautomeric states, predicts hydrogen positions for 4.6M compounds in hours and flags 126 misassigned ligands in the Protein Data Bank (Chemical Science).
items.title: Tautomer-Predictor AI Tool Identifies Stable Molecules for Drug Discovery

items.excerpt: A complexity analysis of games finds grandmasters simplify positions after the opening to cut cognitive load, while chess AIs sustain high strategic tension far longer — and games are decided during the buildup of complexity (APS Open Science).
items.title: Chess Reveals Differences Between Human and AI Strategies

items.excerpt: 25 University of Washington materials-science teams used Ai2's AutoDiscovery agent, which proposes hypotheses, runs analyses and ranks findings by Bayesian surprise, surfacing leads while showing human judgment matters more.
items.title: Teaching future scientists to interrogate AI tools for scientific discovery

items.excerpt: A crowdsourced game built on open model Olmo 3 showed how people exploit unexpected model behaviors to break prosocial AI evaluations, and how open access to internals explains why the tests fail.
items.title: What a crowdsourced game revealed about steering Olmo 3

items.excerpt: After an OpenAI model presented a possible Navier-Stokes solution, mathematicians speculate which Millennium Prize problem AI might crack next.
items.title: Which million-dollar math problem could AI solve next?

items.excerpt: Artificial general intelligence was once confined to technical papers; SciAm examines how the term's meaning has slipped as labs claim it is near.
items.title: AI labs are claiming “AGI” is imminent—but does that mean what we think it means?

items.excerpt: A psychology blog argues humans possess 'story intelligence' that LLMs cannot match. (Opinion/blog.)
items.title: What Can Humans Do That AI Can’t?

items.excerpt: Generative AI has supercharged papermills; publishers are deploying detection tools and new integrity checks to fight fabricated research.
items.title: How scientific publishers are fighting back against fraudulent papermills

items.excerpt: UW–Madison engineers designed a theoretical quantum-emitter nanostructure that supplies the nonlinear operations needed for energy-efficient optical neural networks.
items.title: Tiny Quantum Nanostructures Could Make AI Less of an Energy Hog
